articles_fetched.summary: Vercel replaced Puppeteer + Chromium (about 50MB, ~4s cold starts, too large for functions) with Satori + resvg-wasm (~500KB) at the edge, claiming ~5x faster TTFB and 160x lower cost; Next.js Conf rendered 100k+ ticket images at ~800ms average. Limitations are only loosely stated (basic CSS layout/typography, fonts and emoji fetched as subsets, edge runtime, beta) and the numbers are Vercel's own.

The current README lists many limits: its own layout engine that may differ from browsers, @font-face/@import/@keyframes ignored, fonts passed as TTF/OTF/WOFF buffers (variable fonts at default instance, no generic families), emoji only via graphemeImages, partial bidi, lineHeight rounded to whole px, and invalid inline styles fail the whole render. It now claims Grid support (except subgrid/masonry), which is newer than the 2022 HN 'subset' comments.

GitHub fills an HTML template from GraphQL data and screenshots it with self-hosted Puppeteer, serving ~2M images/day with ~40% cache hits at ~280ms average. The big wins were replacing networkidle0 with a custom wait for fonts/images (2.25s -> 600ms) and giving containers more than 512MB so Chromium avoids a slow low-memory mode.
